rubric_notes: All five families with correct sunids verified against children evidence; fold a.22 single superfamily verified. Correct level semantics (class no homology, fold structural, superfamily common ancestor, family closest) and identifies archaeal and bacterial members as superfamily-level rather than family-level relatives. Explicitly refuses to transfer function between families (core histone to TAF or bacterial protein) and treats a.22.1.0 as bookkeeping. Name-match exclusions supported by search evidence; 'not evolutionarily related' is a mild overstatement. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct sccs, family/superfamily sunids, names, species, 7-93 boundary. Lowest shared node superfamily, interpreted as inferred probable common origin, not sequence-level; explicitly rejects HisE and MazG function/EC/pathway transfer, templates, residue correspondence, orthology; Li/UNL noted as crystallographic ligand not substrate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Superfamily 53067, fold, class, families 53068/53083/53089, other families and the duplication annotation are all bundle-supported (resolve, children, parents, annotations). Correct superfamily-level common ancestry with conserved two-lobe core, and rejection of substrate, function, mechanism, annotation, catalytic-residue and loop/interface transfer; fold alone correctly not treated as homology. Omits the gold-named limits on regulation and oligomeric state. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Family/superfamily/fold identifiers correct and bundle-supported; remote-homology interpretation, chemistry divergence, and transfer limits (family-level sequence and active-site conservation needed, template caveats, intra-family variation) all present. One hierarchy misstatement: claims 'the superfamily and fold nodes are the same group', but fold a.25 contains several superfamilies (a.25.2 through a.25.6 in 2.08); noncentral to the three-family relationship but factually wrong and unsupported by its bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct b.6.1.1/b.6.1.5/b.6.1.6 under b.6.1 with sunids, sibling families and the superfamily copper comment supported by bundle and interpreted correctly. States superfamily as a common-ancestry call, distinguishes from family-level homology, rejects copper/electron-transfer inference and names needed evidence (conserved ligand residues, metal-binding data, family-level homology). Example domains d1ikop_, d5n0ya1, d5n0ma1 and PAD4 sibling domains are not in its bundle but are correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families/superfamily/fold/class with sunids, bundle-supported. Shared scaffold and probable distant ancestry at superfamily level, family split as functional divergence; explicitly rejects conjugation, UBX->p97/RBD->Ras from fold alone, partner/pathway transfer, and ortholog-level template use; flags automated matches and that functional descriptions are background knowledge.

Correct hierarchy with supported sunids (52172, 52171, 51349, 52173, 52252, 82344) and KaiA domains d1r8ja2 and d1m2ea_; homology_implied_by_level=true supported. Interprets superfamily as distant common ancestry, not family-level; rejects phospho-signaling, catalysis, PLP binding, and template transfer; notes wing is one domain of a larger enzyme and KaiA clock role cannot be inferred from fold. Noncentral factual imprecision: says ODC decarboxylase activity belongs to a 'separate C-terminal barrel domain', whereas the Lactobacillus ODC carrying the c.23.1.4 wing has its PLP major domain in c.67.1.5 and a non-barrel d.125.1.1 C-terminal domain. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct placement and identifiers supported by bundle, including homology_implied_by_level scope sf and example domains with boundaries. Explains superfamily criterion vs fold-level similarity, states homology asserted only within b.84.5, explicitly notes placement does not claim independent origin (ancestry unproven, not denied), and rejects functional transfer. Minor: 'I found no sequence or functional link' is slightly stronger than the evidence, but hedged elsewhere. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy (f.21 in class f; f.21.1/81342, f.21.2/81343, f.21.3/103501) supported by the sccs, parents and children responses. Clear fold-vs-superfamily semantics, convergence or undetectably distant relationship both raised and left open, function/heme-geometry/template transfer rejected, and the extra evidence needed (sequence/profile links, conserved heme-ligating residues, curated reclassification) named. No unsupported claims. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families/sunids/superfamily/fold supported by bundle. Superfamily = probable common origin from structural evidence, remote; separate families = low sequence similarity and distinct function. Explicitly denies that shared fold or superfamily shows same ligand, cofactor specificity, mechanism or biological role; distinguishes cofactor-binding half of ADH, acyl-CoA chemistry context, and non-catalytic regulatory RCK domain. Template and representative caveats include domain architecture. Acknowledges no domain SIDs retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct family k.40.1.1 (sunid 100905) and full lineage with identifiers; reasonable 'not in the evolutionary sense' conclusion and transfer limits. Does not retrieve or cite the family's 'not a true family' comment; the override is inferred only from class k. Suggests designs are 'better described as analogous or convergent', which is not supported by the retrieved data. Bio ceiling 2 for ignoring the decisive annotation; factual 2.

2.08 placement correct with sunids (52309 superfamily; families 110461 vs 52310; d1t1ja1 as current SID) and remote-homolog interpretation with fold-vs-superfamily distinction and no function transfer. 1.69 side is unverified recall, explicitly uncertain whether separate fold or superfamily, so c.137.1.1 own-fold placement is missing; wrongly claims the tools only serve SCOPe releases.

d1a14h2 sunid 343393 H:1-8 class l Tags lineage N-terminal Tags/Synthetic l.1.1.1 supported; d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 VH lineage supported; homology warning quoted. Statement that homology_implied_by_level is true for d1a14h1 is not in this bundle but is correct. Rejects tag similarity as homology, directs inference to VH and L-chain domains, recommends excluding tag residues. Complete.

2.08 split correct with good module reasoning and per-domain search guidance. The 1.75 before-state is unverified and hedged as whole-chain or multi-domain, which muddies the historical change and brushes the must-avoid about claiming two early domains. The 3tewA 96.9 percent claim is absent from its bundle (revisions and 2.08 parents only).

Identifiers, boundaries and lineages correct; new fold and mosaic conclusion present with function-transfer caveats. Asserts 'the five domains are not homologous to each other' and that the whole protein 'has no single ancestor', which SCOPe's different-superfamily placements do not establish. Also states every domain has 'only a distant, superfamily-level relationship', incorrect for the family-level bromodomain placement a.29.2.1. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Strong: supported lengths 51/373/752, lineage, 're' flag, 'single repeat', canonical repeat unit with coordinate caveat, good limits. One imprecision: first states all three carry the 're' flag, then correctly notes d4cj9a_ has no inconsistency flag; the evidence shows the flag only on d2kq5a_ and d3v6pa_.

Correctly reports stable 2.08 / 2.08-stable and periodic 2.08-2026-08-16 (bundle-supported; suite frozen value is 2023-01-06, not penalized). Correctly says periodic is not a new stable release and warns against relying on 'current'. However it inverts the citation semantics: recommends the dated periodic identifier as the primary reproducible citation and calls the bare stable label 'a moving reference', which is wrong (the stable release is frozen; the periodic layer moves). Omits that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable-release domains. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. All three structures correctly placed in a.47.2.1 with correct lineage names, sunids, protein nodes and the 'automated match to d3c98b_' comment. Quotes the 'three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat' comment and the 'ms' flag, and explicitly ties the full domain's fourth helix to resolving the spectrin-repeat resemblance (must_include 2). Correctly separates fold-level similarity from superfamily/family homology, rejects function/template transfer from fragments, and treats the automated-match distinction as process not biology. Odd phrase 'e.200s-style' is harmless. Historical caveat honestly stated.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Cited nodes (c.2/c.2.1, c.2.1.9, c.2.1.8, c.3/c.3.1, d.58.20 class d) match the bundle. States convergence or independent origin as likelier across folds but adds that SCOPe does not prove independent origins and some folds may be distantly related, and that the c.2/c.3 relationship is unestablished. Divergence within superfamily, motif weakness, integrated evidence and transfer limits covered. Minor wording slip ('superfamily level and above') contradicted by the rest of the answer, not material.

Chain-B focused but accurate: 2.04 b.23.2.1 CUB-like vs b.18.1.3, 2.08 both in superfamily b.18.1 as families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3. Correctly states fold similarity alone is not proof, combines topology, functional-module context and curator judgment, and rejects transferring function. Thorough limits section.

Lineage, sunids, boundaries, comments, and domain-level non-inherited hf definition match the bundle. Homology retained at family and superfamily level; hf correctly read as different fold despite similar sequence/SS count; template and training caveats (label noise, held-out/weighted separately), no transfer of function or mutant effects; explicitly notes its conformational reading is unverified. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Correctly frames fr as completeness caveat not reclassification; homology retained. Alignment: gaps, shortened coverage, distorted identity/RMSD, align only over present residues. Representative: complete non-flagged domains preferred, d1o5dt2 only as fallback with explicit fragment statement; quality to be checked separately. Diversity: fragment counted at protein level but not as full structural unit; sensitivity check. Lineage, boundaries, fr annotation, comment and protein sunids all supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation; family = clear ancestry plus superfamily-level homology; new fold = different arrangement/connectivity, not small decorations; superfamily placement described as the evolutionary hypothesis, revisable with sequence/structure/function evidence; clarifies new superfamily does not assert non-homology; FATCAT scores are candidate evidence only. Brief wording 'treated as an independent lineage' is immediately qualified. No fabricated facts. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correctly places d.144.1.7, d.144.1.6 and d.144.1.4 (plus siblings) in superfamily d.144.1 in 2.08, supported by the bundle. States that the superfamily (not just the fold) supports homology and a shared ATP-cleft phosphotransfer core, rejects substrate, regulation, residue-equivalence, template and activity transfer including from FATCAT/AlphaFold hits, and requires same-family alignment covering activation segment and specificity loops, biochemistry, complex structures, in vivo data and orthology. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
